Filter Health Data by Demographic Variables

Source: R/sus_data_filter_demographics.R
sus_data_filter_demographics.Rd

Filters health data based on demographic characteristics such as sex, race, age range, education level, region, and municipality. This function complements sus_data_filter_cid() by enabling stratified analyses by population subgroups.

Usage

sus_data_filter_demographics(
  df,
  sex = NULL,
  race = NULL,
  age_range = NULL,
  education = NULL,
  region = NULL,
  city = NULL,
  municipality_code = NULL,
  drop_ignored = FALSE,
  backend = "arrow",
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df at stage "stand" or later (see sus_data_standardize()), or a lazy Arrow/DuckDB table. Must be standardized so that the demographic columns can be found.

sex

Character scalar or vector of sex labels to keep, e.g. "Female", c("Masculino", "Feminino"). Must match the labels of the standardized column in the language used in sus_data_standardize() (English Male/Female; Portuguese Masculino/Feminino; Spanish Masculino/Femenino); input is converted to title case. NULL (default) keeps all. If no sex column is found, a warning is issued and the filter is skipped.

race

Character scalar or vector of race/color labels to keep, e.g. "Parda", c("Branca", "Preta") (IBGE categories, see Details), matched against the standardized column in the same way as sex. NULL (default) keeps all. Skipped with a warning if no race column is found.

age_range

Numeric vector of length 2, c(min_age, max_age) in years, both ends inclusive, e.g. c(0, 4), c(65, Inf) (Inf = no upper limit). NULL (default) keeps all ages. Requires an age_years column, created by sus_data_create_variables(); the function aborts if it is missing or if the length is not 2.

education

Character scalar or vector of education labels to keep (as they appear in the standardized column, title-cased). NULL (default) keeps all. Skipped with a warning if no education column is found.

region

Character or numeric scalar/vector, default NULL. State(s) to keep, given as region/biome names (e.g. "norte", "amazonia_legal", "matopiba"; PT/EN/ES aliases such as "north" accepted; see Details), UF abbreviations ("SP", c("RJ", "ES")) or IBGE state codes (35). The elements are combined (union). Matching uses the state column of the data (e.g. manager/notification UF), not municipality of residence. Aborts if no valid state results.

city

Character vector of municipality names (e.g., "Sao Paulo", "Natal") or IBGE codes (6 or 7-digit, e.g., "3550308", "2408102"). Case-insensitive; accents are normalised for matching. Partial typos trigger fuzzy suggestions. If NULL (default), no additional municipality filter is applied. Results are merged (union) with any codes in municipality_code.

municipality_code

Character or numeric vector of IBGE municipality codes (6 or 7 digits), e.g. c(3550308, 3304557). Combined (union) with city. NULL (default) keeps all municipalities.

drop_ignored

Logical scalar, default FALSE. If TRUE, rows with NA or DATASUS "ignored" codes ("Ignorado", "9", "99", "unknown", ...) in the columns of the requested sex/race/education filters are removed.

backend

Character scalar, "arrow" (default) or "tibble". "arrow" filters lazily and falls back to "tibble" (in memory) with a warning if it fails; "tibble" processes in memory.

use_cache

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Cache the municipality metadata used to resolve city/municipality_code; only relevant then.

cache_dir

Character scalar, directory of the cache, default "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial".

lang

Character scalar, "pt" (default), "en" or "es". Language of messages; other values abort.

verbose

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Print the filtering summary.

Value

A climasus_df with only the rows meeting all the given criteria (lazy if the input was lazy and arrow succeeded); columns are unchanged. sus_meta: stage = "filter_demo", type = "filter_demo", with the applied filters recorded in the history.

Details

Pipeline position: after sus_data_filter_cid() (or directly after sus_data_standardize()); age_range needs sus_data_create_variables() first. All filters are combined with AND; NULL arguments are skipped.

The function automatically detects column names in different languages and standardisations. It handles both original DATASUS column names and standardised names from sus_data_standardize().

Sex categories (case-insensitive):

  • English: "Male", "Female"

  • Portuguese: "Masculino", "Feminino"

  • Spanish: "Masculino", "Femenino"

Race/Color categories (IBGE standard):

  • English: "White", "Black", "Yellow", "Brown", "Indigenous"

  • Portuguese: "Branca", "Preta", "Amarela", "Parda", "Indigena"

  • Spanish: "Blanca", "Negra", "Amarilla", "Parda", "Indigena"

Regions accepted by region:

IBGE Macro-regions:

  • "norte": c("AC", "AP", "AM", "PA", "RO", "RR", "TO")

  • "nordeste": c("AL", "BA", "CE", "MA", "PB", "PE", "PI", "RN", "SE")

  • "centro_oeste": c("DF", "GO", "MT", "MS")

  • "sudeste": c("ES", "MG", "RJ", "SP")

  • "sul": c("PR", "RS", "SC")

Biomes (Ecological Borders):

  • "amazonia_legal": c("AC", "AP", "AM", "PA", "RO", "RR", "MT", "MA", "TO")

  • "mata_atlantica": c("AL", "BA", "CE", "ES", "GO", "MA", "MG", "MS", "PB", "PE", "PI", "PR", "RJ", "RN", "RS", "SC", "SE", "SP")

  • "caatinga": c("AL", "BA", "CE", "MA", "PB", "PE", "PI", "RN", "SE", "MG")

  • "cerrado": c("BA", "DF", "GO", "MA", "MG", "MS", "MT", "PA", "PI", "PR", "RO", "SP", "TO")

  • "pantanal": c("MT", "MS")

  • "pampa": c("RS")

Hydrography & Climate:

  • "bacia_amazonia": c("AC", "AM", "AP", "MT", "PA", "RO", "RR")

  • "bacia_sao_francisco": c("AL", "BA", "DF", "GO", "MG", "PE", "SE")

  • "bacia_parana": c("GO", "MG", "MS", "PR", "SP")

  • "bacia_tocantins": c("GO", "MA", "PA", "TO")

  • "semi_arido": c("AL", "BA", "CE", "MA", "PB", "PE", "PI", "RN", "SE", "MG")

Health, Agriculture & Geopolitics:

  • "matopiba": c("MA", "TO", "PI", "BA")

  • "arco_desmatamento": c("RO", "AC", "AM", "PA", "MT", "MA")

  • "dengue_hyperendemic": c("GO", "MS", "MT", "PR", "RJ", "SP")

  • "sudene": c("AL", "BA", "CE", "MA", "PB", "PE", "PI", "RN", "SE", "MG", "ES")

  • "fronteira_brasil": c("AC", "AM", "AP", "MT", "MS", "PA", "PR", "RO", "RR", "RS", "SC")

See also

sus_data_filter_cid(), sus_data_create_variables(), sus_data_standardize()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(climasus4r)

# Filter by sex only (labels follow the language used in standardize)
df_women <- sus_data_filter_demographics(df, sex = "Feminino", lang = "pt")

# Filter by age range (elderly, 65+); needs age_years from
# sus_data_create_variables()
df_elderly <- sus_data_filter_demographics(df, age_range = c(65, Inf))

# Filter by city name (with accent tolerance)
df_natal <- sus_data_filter_demographics(df, city = "Natal", lang = "pt")

# Filter by multiple city names
df_capitals <- sus_data_filter_demographics(
  df,
  city = c("Sao Paulo", "Rio de Janeiro", "Fortaleza"), #Usar acentos se preferir
  lang = "pt"
)

# Mix: city names + explicit codes (union)
df_subset <- sus_data_filter_demographics(
  df,
  city            = "Natal",
  municipality_code = "3550308",
  lang            = "pt"
)

# Complex filtering
df_children <- sus_data_filter_demographics(
  df,
  age_range = c(0, 5),
  region    = "norte",
  lang      = "pt"
)
} # }
